title: Its ai completing classic games something you would watch
author: AttitudeDecent9223
selftext: Like it says on the title i run a very small gaming channel about precisely that, the ai taking games such as yu gi oh forbidden memories, age of empires II and more that i plan to add in the future, but as the videos get out i feel the numbers are not there, is this something that doesnt have a good audience? I would really love some feedback, the channel is in my profile description, thanks in advance

comments.author: blunt4brains
comments.body: Probably because no one wants to watch a computer play a video game. What is enjoyable about watching that ?

replies.author: AttitudeDecent9223
replies.body: To me its more about the cuestionable decisions it makes, you can imagine that the ai plays in a weird way , when i wach it i feel like if im couching a younger cousin that doesnt have a clue jaja

replies.author: MongolianMudPie
replies.body: I thought the same 15 years ago. Who wants to watch others play when you could play instead? But there seem to be people who prefer watching, otherwise streamers would not be so successful.

replies.author: blunt4brains
replies.body: People watch streamers for their personality and the parasocial aspect.  That doesn't exist with Ai playing games . Really not a good comparison

replies.author: AttitudeDecent9223
replies.body: Im with you about the streamers i dont like them myself, my videos are more about recording it play and then edit all the boring parts out giving it a voice etc is not just the ai and nothing else, if not it would be boring jaja

comments.author: Lucko_Coldwolf
comments.body: Let me talk to your mom.

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body:
I never understood people who watch human streamers play games to begin with, I do understand it if it was a review and you were trying to see whether the game is worth getting or not but that's about it.

Now to watch AI play a game... that could be interesting for like 2 seconds just as something novel, but do I want to go past like 2 mins of it? that's a big no for me. I'm not your target audiance though, not entirely sure who would be to be honest.

replies.author: AttitudeDecent9223
replies.body:
Im with you about the streamers, i never saw the point, too noisy as well, i dont do streams neither the videos i make, i record the ai play and them edit all the slow parts out , since it takes a while for it to think i also edit in, an avatar and a voice for it, it takes a bit

Its more about the ai being a questionable player and the old games being dificult, but yeah still trying to find that audience though, thanks for the reply mate

comments.author: derLeisemitderLaute
comments.body: DougDoug once let [ChatGPT play PyjamaSam](https://youtu.be/W3id8E34cRQ?si=DQCuOj1czLnKWm2F) and it is one of my favourite videos ever. That video also got a lot of views, so yes, there is an audience for that. Its mostly about how you do it.

comments.author: DatabaseNearby5
comments.body:
I made a channel for specifically Sim City 2000 gameplay. After about two months I have 30 subscribers, \~20k views and \~53 watch hours in the last month. “Views” is pretty loose though, someone watching a short for 5 seconds counts. It’s not a lot but it’s growing slowly.

At first I was just playing around with a gameplay harness then I figured I might as well try putting it on YouTube. I do sometimes wonder if I’m just contributing to slopifying the platform, but at least a couple people seem to like it (the videos are very low key, AI mostly seems to slowly crush their city economy by taking out loans… should probably tell them to stop but I’m waiting to see if they end up bankrupting the city)
